title: East Bengal Stun Al-Arabi 4-1 to Reach AFC Champions League Two Group Stage
excerpt: The ISL champions came from behind with a dramatic 90th-minute equaliser and three extra-time goals to beat Kuwaits Al-Arabi SC at a packed Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata, booking their place in the AFC Champions League Two main round.
body:
• East Bengal FC came from behind to beat Al-Arabi SC 4-1 after extra time in the AFC Champions League Two Preliminary Stage at Kolkatas Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan.
  • Jay Gupta headed in a 90th-minute equaliser from captain MD Basim Rashids free kick after Al-Arabi had taken the lead through an Iwuala penalty in the 76th minute.
  • Rashid, David Himar, and Rohit Danu each scored in extra time to complete a dominant comeback and secure a spot in the ACL Two group stage.
  • The result marks a landmark moment for Indian club football on the continental stage, while FC Goa were eliminated after a 0-3 loss to FK Arkadag.

Al-Arabi Strike First Against the Run of Play

East Bengal FC dominated from the opening whistle at a packed Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata on Tuesday night, but it was Kuwaits Al-Arabi SC who drew first blood. The ISL champions controlled possession and created the better chances throughout the first half, with captain MD Basim Rashid testing Al-Arabi goalkeeper Sulaiman Abdulghafoor with a long-range effort as early as the sixth minute.

The visitors defended resolutely and threatened on the counter through their pacy wingers. Al-Arabis Maleko had the best chance of the first half when he headed wide from a Y. Majed cross inside the box.

East Bengal continued to press after the break. Bipin Singh missed a golden opportunity from inside the box in the 50th minute after Jesin TK set him up cleanly. The game turned in the 74th minute when defender Sandip Mandi dragged down Maleko inside the area, and referee pointed to the spot. Iwuala converted the penalty in the 76th minute, giving Al-Arabi a lead that appeared increasingly harsh on the dominant hosts.

Jay Guptas Header Rescues East Bengal

With the clock running down and elimination looming, East Bengal found their lifeline. In the 90th minute, captain Rashid delivered a perfectly placed free kick into the box, and Jay Gupta rose to meet it with a powerful header that found the back of the net. The Salt Lake Stadium erupted.

"East Bengal FC secured a great comeback victory against Al-Arabi SC as they secured the spot in the ACL Two."

— Khel Now

The equaliser sent the match into extra time, where East Bengal were utterly dominant. Al-Arabi, who had spent most of the 90 minutes defending, had nothing left to offer going forward.

Three Extra-Time Goals Seal Historic Win

The Red and Gold broke Al-Arabis resistance in the 108th minute. Rohit Danu played a pass that deflected into the path of Rashid, who struck a sweet half-volley from an acute angle to put East Bengal ahead for the first time.

David Himar, who had come off the bench, made it 3-1 in the 116th minute, toying with the tiring Kuwaiti defence before finishing clinically. Rohit Danu then added the fourth after PV Vishnu played him through inside the box, and the young forward made no mistake.

The 4-1 scoreline secured East Bengals place in the AFC Champions League Two group stage — a significant achievement for Indian club football and a result that drew comparisons to the clubs famous 6-2 comeback victory over Iraqs Al-Zawraa in the 1993-94 Asian Cup Winners Cup at the same venue.

FC Goa Bow Out

In the other ACL Two Preliminary Stage match involving an Indian club, FC Goa were comprehensively beaten 3-0 by Turkmenistans FK Arkadag and were eliminated from the competition. Goa will now drop into the AFC Challenge League.

East Bengals progression means at least one Indian club will compete in the ACL Two group stage this season, keeping the countrys continental football ambitions alive. For the Indian football diaspora and fans worldwide, the result at Salt Lake was a reminder that Indian club football can compete on the Asian stage when it matters most.
